BiblicalUsage: Perash means to specify, to make plain. The king told the Jews that the letter they sent had been plainly read before him — every word of it weighed.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that God hears what is plainly read: the letter was read before the king, and every letter is read before Him.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
